modelSelector.title: Extraction model
modelSelector.description: Choose which Gemini model analyzes your papers.

default.title: Default
default.description: Tries the newest, most capable model first, then automatically falls back to a faster or cheaper one if it runs out of quota mid-batch.
default.warning: The model used can change partway through the batch due to rate limits — check the "Model Used" column in the export to see what actually ran on each paper.

flash.title: gemini-3.5-flash
flash.description: The best balance of accuracy and speed. Recommended for most batches.

lite.title: gemini-3.5-flash-lite
lite.description: Fastest and cheapest, but more prone to reasoning mistakes such as layer order or internal consistency.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.abstractBody: λLens is a research tool built during a Yonsei University Photonics Lab internship to speed up how the lab surveys the literature on integrated photonic sensors. Pulling figure-of-merit values — resonance wavelength, sensitivity, Q-factor, FWHM — out of papers by hand does not scale past a handful of references. λLens combines a guided PDF-extraction pipeline with an interactive visualization workspace, so a researcher can go from a folder of papers to a filterable, exportable comparison chart in minutes rather than days.
intro.guideBody: This guide documents Mode 1 (Excel-to-Plot visualization), which is complete and ready to use — see the table of contents on the next page. Mode 2 (PDF extraction and validation) is still under active development and will be documented here once it stabilizes.
intro.authorBody: λLens was developed by Danaé A.M. as part of a research internship at the Yonsei University Photonics Lab.

toc.title: Table of contents
toc.hint: Click any entry to jump to that page.

scenario.title: Worked example used throughout this section
scenario.body: The screenshots below all come from one running example: six all-dielectric photonic resonator sensor designs (silicon and silicon-nitride rings, a guided-mode resonance grating, a silicon disk on a dielectric Bragg mirror, an InP interferometer, and a polymer ring), each reported once from measurement (EXP) and once from simulation (SIM). We compare their FOM (Sensitivity / FWHM) against resonance wavelength.

import.title: 1. Import your dataset
import.overviewBody: Once a file is loaded, the workspace has three parts: a control panel on the left (axes, display, filters), the scatter chart in the middle, and a right-hand panel for comparing groups and annotating points. Every one of them is documented in this guide.
import.body: From the Visualization tool, drop an Excel or CSV file onto the dropzone below, or click it to browse for one.
import.figure1Caption: Figure 1 — The import dropzone: drag an Excel or CSV file here, or click to browse (.xlsx, .xls, .csv, up to 10 MB).
import.figure2Caption: Figure 2 — The workspace toolbar once a file is loaded.

import.label: Import
import.body: opens the dropzone again to load a different file, replacing the current dataset.

export.label: Export
export.body: offers the filtered dataset as CSV or Excel, or the chart as a PNG image (see page 9).

reset.label: Reset
reset.body: restores the default axes, display options and filters for the loaded dataset, without re-importing it.

controls.title: 2. Axes and display options
controls.body: The Chart section (top) picks what gets plotted; the Display section (below it) controls how it's drawn. Only one section is expanded at a time — click a section's header to switch.

title.label: Chart title
title.body: an optional name shown above the chart — useful before a PNG export.

yAxis.label: Y-Axis
yAxis.body: the numeric column plotted vertically, e.g. FOM or Q-factor. Only numeric columns are offered.

xAxis.label: X-Axis
xAxis.body: the column plotted horizontally — numeric or categorical, depending on what the sheet contains.

scale.label: Scale
scale.body: toggles the Y axis between logarithmic and linear — log keeps values that span several orders of magnitude readable.

trendLine.label: Trend line
trendLine.body: fits a straight line through the plotted points. Needs a numeric X axis with at least two distinct values.

pareto.label: Pareto frontier
pareto.body: highlights the non-dominated points — records not beaten on both axes by any other point.

legend.label: Show legend
legend.body: draws the group colors (and any trend/Pareto overlay) on the chart itself, so they're included in a PNG export.

median.label: Median line
median.body: draws a dashed line at the median value of the Y axis currently plotted.

filters.title: 3. Filters
filters.body: Filters narrow the dataset down without changing the underlying file — unchecking a chip hides that value everywhere (chart, stats, exports) until it's checked again. They only appear when the sheet actually has a matching column.
filters.figureCaption: Figure 5 — The Filters section, showing Origin, Material Class and Base Materials for our worked example.
filters.note: Material Class and Base Materials are "composite" filters: a cell like "Dielectric;Semiconductor" counts toward both chips at once, and unchecking either one drops any row that lists it, even combined with something else.

origin.label: Origin
origin.body: includes or excludes experimental (EXP) and simulated (SIM) records.

materialClass.label: Material Class
materialClass.body: filters by material category — a combined cell counts toward every category it lists.

baseMaterials.label: Base Materials
baseMaterials.body: filters by specific material (Si, SiN, Ta2O5, ...) — same combined-cell handling as Material Class.

reading.title: 4. Reading and interacting with the chart
reading.body: Every point is one reported record. Colors follow the current "Group / Color by" column — here, Origin.
reading.figure4Caption: Figure 6 — The scatter chart for our worked example: FOM (Y, log scale) against resonance wavelength (X), colored by Origin — orange for EXP, blue for SIM — with the median line and legend visible.

badges.label: Status badges
badges.body: sample count, the EXP/SIM breakdown, and how many points are flagged for review.

legend.label: Legend
legend.body: one color per group — in the live app, clicking an entry isolates that series.

median.label: Median line
median.body: the dashed line marking the median value of the axis currently plotted.

hover.label: Hover
hover.body: shows the full wavelength, Q-factor and other metrics for a point.

zoom.label: Scroll / drag
zoom.body: zooms and pans inside the plot to inspect a region closely.

click.label: Click
click.body: pins a point so it can be compared later — see the next page.

compare.title: 5. Compare groups
compare.body: The Compare groups panel summarizes whatever column is picked as "Group / Color by" — here, Origin — with per-group statistics that always match exactly what the chart is showing.
compare.figureCaption: Figure 7 — The Compare groups panel, showing EXP and SIM.

groupBySelect.label: Group / Color by
groupBySelect.body: picks which column splits the chart (and this panel) into colored groups.

groupCard.label: Group card
groupCard.body: click to isolate that group on the chart (dims the rest); the chevron expands n, mean, median and σ.

compare.note: Mean, median and σ only appear once a group has at least 3 points — below that, they'd describe individual values rather than a real distribution.

annotate.title: 6. Pin and annotate points
annotate.body: Clicking any chart point pins it here as a card — a lightweight, session-only bookmark for comparing a handful of specific records without the rest of the dataset competing for attention.
annotate.figureCaption: Figure 8 — The Annotations panel with two pinned points, one of them flagged for review.

sort.label: Sort
sort.body: orders pinned cards by when they were added, or by their reference.

showOnlyPinned.label: Show only pinned points
showOnlyPinned.body: narrows the chart and the Compare groups panel down to exactly the pinned rows.

card.label: Pinned card
card.body: reference, title, plotted axis values, and an editable note — pre-filled from the sheet's Notes/Evidence columns when available.

annotate.extra: Expanding a card also surfaces a "pin this paper's other rows" shortcut when siblings exist, a Layer Structure viewer, and a Metrics box — each with its own zoom dialog and a dedicated PNG export (see the next page).

export.title: 7. Export your results
export.body: Everything in Mode 1 can leave the app in a form you can reuse elsewhere: the filtered dataset as a spreadsheet, the chart as an image, and any pinned point's details as a small standalone PNG or text file.
export.chartCaption: Figure 9 — The chart image export, produced by "Export → Chart image (.png)" — a title, trend line and Pareto frontier have been turned on to show the full range of what can go into it.
export.pinExportCaption: Figure 10 — One pinned point's full export, produced by "Export this pin" — everything on the card (Origin, Mode, a multi-layer structure, Metrics and the note) combined into a single PNG.

formats.csv: the filtered rows as a CSV file.
formats.xlsx: the filtered rows as an Excel workbook.
formats.png: the chart exactly as displayed, including title, legend and any overlay.

pinFormats.note: the note text, as its own .txt file.
pinFormats.fields: the Metrics box (or Layer Structure) as a small, self-contained PNG image.
pinFormats.all: everything on the card — Mode, structure, metrics and note — as one combined PNG.

useCases.title: 8. Example use cases
useCases.intro: A few ways the controls above combine in practice, using the same worked example.

compareExpSim.title: Checking measurement against simulation
compareExpSim.body: Keep both Origin values checked, group by Origin, and turn on the median line: if the EXP median sits well below the SIM one, simulations may be systematically optimistic for this dataset.

reviewFlagged.title: Triaging records that need a second look
reviewFlagged.body: The "flagged for review" badge marks records whose FWHM was estimated rather than read directly. Pin one, open its note, and check the estimation method before trusting the value.

publicationFigure.title: Preparing a figure for a paper
publicationFigure.body: Filter down to the material platforms you're comparing, turn on the legend and axis markers for clarity, then export the chart as a PNG — it's already sized and labeled for reuse.

comingSoon.title: Coming soon
comingSoon.body: The PDF extraction and validation workflow is still under active development. This guide will be updated with full documentation once that feature is ready.

rules.title: AI extraction rules
rules.body: Gemini will read each paper against a fixed set of business rules — substrate checks, wavelength-domain validation — before proposing a value for review.

validation.title: Human-in-the-loop validation
validation.body: A split-screen view will let you approve, edit or exclude each extracted value next to its source page before it's added to your dataset.

workspace.title: Analysis workspace
workspace.pinHint: Click a point to pin an annotation

stats.title: Compare groups

tooltips.n: Count of points from this group plotted on the chart.
tooltips.mean: Average of the plotted Y-axis values for this group.
tooltips.median: Middle plotted Y-axis value for this group. Matches the dashed median line when this group is isolated.
tooltips.std: Standard deviation of this group's plotted Y-axis values: how spread out they are around the mean.

stats.isolate: Isolate this group on the chart (doesn't affect the stats)

annotations.title: Annotations
annotations.tooltip: Click any point to pin it here. Check 2 or more pins to compare them.
annotations.empty: No pins yet — click any point on the chart to bookmark it for later comparison.
annotations.showOnlyPinnedTooltip: Hides every point except the ones pinned below. Stats narrow down to this same selection too.

compare.title: Compare pinned points
compare.description: Pick which sections to include and, optionally, a title for this comparison image.
compare.hint: Select 2 to {max} pinned points to compare them.
compare.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Ring resonators vs. grating sensors
compare.empty: Pick at least one section to include.

tooltips.groupBy: Colors points by this column so you can compare groups at a glance.
tooltips.scale: Log keeps values that span several orders of magnitude readable. Linear keeps equal spacing between values.
tooltips.legend: Draws the legend on the chart itself, so it's included when exporting as an image.
tooltips.median: Draws a dashed line at the median Y value of the points plotted.
tooltips.trendLine: Fits a curve through the points to show the overall trend. Needs a numeric X axis; "Auto" picks whichever shape fits best.
tooltips.trendType: The mathematical model the trend line fits (linear, exponential, logarithmic, power, or polynomial). "Auto" keeps whichever has the highest R².
tooltips.pareto: Highlights the non-dominated points — not beaten on both axes by any other point.
tooltips.trendUnavailable: Needs at least 2 points with different X values to draw anything.
tooltips.exclusionMode: Strict excludes a point as soon as it contains one unchecked material/class. Lenient only excludes it once ALL of its materials/classes are unchecked.
tooltips.mergeMultiCategory: A multi-category point normally plots once per category. Turn this on to show a single gradient marker instead.
